files.rules/ingest-alerts-failed-transform.yam:
# I-3.a · the SIEM base adapter logs one WARNING per batch with dropped alerts
# that failed to transform, then moves the cursor past them.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.alerts-failed-transform
title: Alerts from a source fail to transform and are skipped
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-3, causes: [I-3.a]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  dropped:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: core.federation.adapters._siem_base}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {eq: '%s dropped %d of %d alert(s) that failed to transform%s'}
when: {fn: count, signal: dropped, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 1}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 15m
advice:
  summary: Vigil skipped some alerts from a source because it couldn't read their format; they won't be fetched again.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident: the
    vendor's alert format has likely changed. If you can, include one sample
    alert from the source's console for this period.
files.rules/ingest-federation-integration-disa:
# I-1.i · the federation row is enabled but its integration is off; the runner
# skips the source (one WARNING per process) and nothing arrives. is_configured is
# "integration enabled" (_siem_base.py:69). Needs sources.is_configured and the
# global switch from the federation sensor.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.federation-integration-disabled
title: Federation source is enabled but its integration is not configured
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-1, causes: [I-1.i]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  federation: {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: global.enabled}}
  enabled:    {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: sources.enabled, by: [source]}}
  configured: {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: sources.is_configured, by: [source]}}
group_by: [source]
when:
  all:
    - {fn: latest, signal: federation, op: "==", value: true}
    - {fn: latest, signal: enabled, op: "==", value: true}
    - {fn: latest, signal: configured, op: "==", value: false}
for: 15m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: A federation source is switched on but its integration is off or unconfigured, so its polls return nothing.
  fix: >-
    In Settings, Integrations either turn the integration on and complete its
    settings, or disable the matching federation source, so the two agree.
# I-3.h · #1613: the runner drops records with no external_id / finding_id and
# counts them per source.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.federation-records-dropped
title: Federation is dropping records it can't identify
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-3, causes: [I-3.h]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  dropped: {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: sources.dropped_total, by: [source]}}
group_by: [source]
when: {fn: increase, signal: dropped, window: 1h, op: ">", value: 0}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 15m
advice:
  summary: Some alerts from this source were dropped because they carry no identifier Vigil can store them under.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident. Dropped
    alerts are not retried; check the source's console for alerts in this period
    that are missing from Vigil.
files.rules/ingest-host-clock-ahead.yaml:
# I-3.g · alerts newer than the host clock cap the federation cursor; with a host
# clock behind, alerts in the gap are skipped. Repeats once per affected batch.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.host-clock-ahead
title: Source alerts are timestamped ahead of the Vigil host clock
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-3, causes: [I-3.g]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  ahead:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: core.federation.adapters._base}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {eq: "Federation %s: newest alert time %s is ahead of this host's clock (window end %s); capping the cursor there"}
when: {fn: count, signal: ahead, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 3}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 30m
advice:
  summary: Alerts keep arriving dated in the future by this host's clock, so Vigil may skip some of them.
  fix: >-
    Check that the Vigil host's clock is right and synchronised (enable NTP or
    chrony). If the clock is right, the source is sending alerts dated in the
    future: check the time settings on the source.
files.rules/ingest-integration-config-incomple:
# I-1.b · #1661 config_gap.py: WARNING on the first skipped poll, then a reminder
# every 60 skipped polls (1 h at a 60 s interval, 5 h at 300 s). Counted over a
# window, not latched: the INFO "complete" line only comes from the daemon process
# that saw the gap (module memory), so it never comes if the admin turns the
# integration off or soc-daemon restarts first, and a set latch never retires.
# The 6 h window covers poll intervals up to 6 min; a site with a longer interval
# should raise reminder_window, or the incident reopens on each reminder.
# Grouping on args[0] makes the rule untrusted.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.integration-config-incomplete
title: SIEM integration is enabled but missing required settings
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-1, causes: [I-1.b]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  incomplete:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {prefix: core.integrations.}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {re2: '^%s configuration (still )?incomplete \(missing: %s\)'}
      keys: {integration: "args[0]"}
group_by: [integration]
when: {fn: count, signal: incomplete, window: {param: reminder_window}, op: ">=", value: 1}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
params:
  reminder_window: {type: duration, default: 6h, min: 1h, max: 48h}
advice:
  summary: An integration is switched on but missing settings, so Vigil skips every poll and no alerts arrive from it.
  fix: >-
    Open Settings, Integrations and fill every required field for this
    integration (Elastic: Elasticsearch URL; OpenSearch: OpenSearch URL;
    Sentinel: client secret, subscription ID, resource group, workspace name;
    Defender: tenant and app credentials), or turn the integration off. Polling
    resumes on its own; this incident closes once the daemon has stopped
    reporting the gap for 6 hours.
files.rules/ingest-kafka-cannot-connect.yaml:
# I-2.g · the consumer can't start (broker list, SASL, CA, ACL) and retries.
# connected is false whenever Kafka is off too, so the retry line corroborates.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.kafka-cannot-connect
title: Kafka consumer can't connect to the broker
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-2, causes: [I-2.g]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  connected: {sample: {signal: daemon_status.kafka, key: connected}}
  start_failed:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: core.ingestion.kafka_consumer_service}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'Kafka consumer failed to start: %s'}
when:
  all:
    - {fn: latest, signal: connected, op: "==", value: false}
    - {fn: count, signal: start_failed, window: 15m, op: ">=", value: 3}
for: 5m
keep_firing_for: 10m
advice:
  summary: The Kafka consumer keeps failing to connect, so no alerts arrive from Kafka.
  fix: >-
    Check the Kafka settings in Settings, Integrations, Kafka: the broker list,
    SASL user and password, CA file, and that the user may read the topic and
    consumer group. Confirm the Vigil host can reach the brokers. If you changed
    the settings in the console, restart soc-daemon so it uses them.
files.rules/ingest-kafka-decode-errors.yaml:
# I-3.j · the Kafka consumer skips messages it can't decode or that lack a
# finding_id, with no dead-letter queue.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.kafka-decode-errors
title: Kafka consumer is skipping malformed messages
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-3, causes: [I-3.j]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  decode_errors: {sample: {signal: daemon_status.kafka, key: decode_errors}}
  missing_id:    {sample: {signal: daemon_status.kafka, key: missing_id_errors}}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: increase, signal: decode_errors, window: 15m, op: ">", value: 5}
    - {fn: increase, signal: missing_id, window: 15m, op: ">", value: 5}
for: 10m
keep_firing_for: 15m
advice:
  summary: Messages from the Kafka topic are dropped because they can't be decoded or have no finding_id.
  fix: >-
    Check the producer that writes to the Vigil Kafka topic. Each message must be
    valid JSON with a finding_id field. Dropped messages are not retried.
files.rules/ingest-optional-sdk-missing.yaml:
# I-1.e · the Security Hub / Sentinel fetch can't import its SDK. Since main made
# these raise, the line repeats every poll; constant text, so catalog-trusted.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.optional-sdk-missing
title: A SIEM integration's Python SDK is not installed
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-1, causes: [I-1.e]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  missing:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {re2: '^core\.integrations\.(aws_security_hub|azure_sentinel)\.ingestion$'}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^(boto3|Azure SDK) not installed\. Install: pip install '}
when: {fn: count, signal: missing, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 1}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: Polls for AWS Security Hub or Azure Sentinel fail because the SDK they need is missing from this install.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident: the Vigil package is missing a
    dependency. On a host-native install you can work around it by installing
    the package the soc-daemon log names (boto3, or azure-mgmt-securityinsight
    and azure-identity) into Vigil's environment and restarting soc-daemon.
files.rules/ingest-processor-store-dropped.yam:
# I-3.d · #1341: a finding whose store fails after the retry is forgotten and
# logged once (%-style). What's left after the fix is "the database rejected
# writes"; who owns the database decides lane 1 or 2, so lane 2 until G1 can tell.
# Any store exception drops, including one malformed finding, hence >= 3.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.processor-store-dropped
title: Daemon processor is dropping findings the database won't store
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-3, causes: [I-3.d]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  dropped:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'Dropped finding %s: database store failed'}
when: {fn: count, signal: dropped, window: 15m, op: ">=", value: 3}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 15m
advice:
  summary: The database refused to store some new findings, so they were dropped and won't be retried.
  fix: >-
    Check Postgres: free disk space, the connection limit, and its log for
    rejected writes. Once it accepts writes, new findings are stored again; the
    dropped ones need to be re-sent from their source. If Postgres is healthy, a
    source may be sending findings Vigil can't store: report it as a Vigil
    defect with this incident.
# I-3.e · the processor started without its database service, so every finding
# takes the drop path (_store_with_retry in services/daemon/processor.py) and federation records each tick as a
# failure. Set by the start-up failure (an f-string, so untrusted), cleared by the
# next start that connects (each start logs exactly one of the two).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.processor-without-database
title: Daemon processor is running without its database
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-3, causes: [I-3.e]}
lane: 2
detection: event
input_trust: untrusted
signals:
  failed:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {prefix: 'Failed to initialize database service: '}
      trusted_only: false
  ready:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {eq: Database service initialized}
when: {fn: latch, set: failed, clear: ready}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: soc-daemon started without reaching the database, so new findings are processed but never stored.
  fix: >-
    Check that Postgres is running and reachable from soc-daemon with the
    configured credentials, then restart soc-daemon. If Vigil runs its own
    bundled Postgres and it is healthy, report it as a Vigil defect with this incident.
files.rules/ingest-source-polls-failing.yaml:
# I-2 · every poll of a source fails (credential, network, rate limit). The
# federation runner keeps the cursor and counts consecutive failures per source.
# I-1.a lands here too since #1605 (a CrowdStrike client that can't be built raises),
# and I-1.g (a failed Splunk query fails the tick). With federation switched off
# globally the runner idles and the error count freezes, so the rule needs the
# global switch from the federation sensor.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.source-polls-failing
title: Enabled source fails on every poll
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-2, causes: [I-1.a, I-1.g, I-2.a, I-2.b, I-2.c, I-2.d]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  federation: {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: global.enabled}}
  enabled: {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: sources.enabled, by: [source]}}
  errors:  {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: sources.consecutive_errors, by: [source]}}
group_by: [source]
when:
  all:
    - {fn: latest, signal: federation, op: "==", value: true}
    - {fn: latest, signal: enabled, op: "==", value: true}
    - {fn: latest, signal: errors, op: ">=", value: {param: min_errors}}
for: 10m
keep_firing_for: 10m
params:
  min_errors: {type: number, default: 3, min: 1, max: 50}
advice:
  summary: Every recent poll of this source has failed, so no alerts are arriving from it. Vigil keeps its place and catches up once polls succeed.
  fix: >-
    Open Settings, Integrations for this source and run Test Connection. If it
    reports an authentication error, replace the credential. For Splunk, also
    check the account can search index=notable. If the host can't
    be reached, check the URL, DNS, firewall, proxy and CA bundle from the Vigil
    host. If the vendor reports a rate limit (429), lengthen the poll interval
    or raise the vendor quota. After changing a credential, restart soc-daemon:
    it keeps the old client until then.
files.rules/ingest-source-silent.yaml:
# I-1 umbrella · polls succeed, nothing arrives. The causes that still return an
# empty, successful fetch at 8f98bdf6 land here (I-1.d inferred, its B5 line is
# gone); the ones that now raise (I-1.a #1605, I-1.e, I-1.k) show as failing polls.
# "Recent success" is 30 min: twice the longest default interval (Security Hub 900 s).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.source-silent
title: Enabled source reports healthy polls but has delivered no findings
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-1, causes: [I-1.d]}
lane: 3
detection: absence
signals:
  enabled:      {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: sources.enabled, by: [source]}}
  last_success: {sample: {signal: federation_sources, key: sources.last_success_at, by: [source]}}
  arrivals:     {sample: {signal: triage, key: sources.arrivals, by: [source]}}
group_by: [source]
when:
  all:
    - {fn: latest, signal: enabled, op: "==", value: true}
    - {fn: age, signal: last_success, op: "<", value: 1800}
    - {fn: increase, signal: arrivals, window: {param: quiet_window}, op: "==", value: 0}
for: 15m
keep_firing_for: 30m
params:
  quiet_window: {type: duration, default: 24h, min: 1h, max: 48h}
advice:
  summary: The source is polled without errors but has sent no findings for the whole quiet window.
  fix: >-
    Check the source's credentials and configuration in Settings, Integrations,
    and confirm the source itself produced alerts in this period. If it did and
    both are correct, report it as a Vigil defect with this incident.
files.rules/ingest-webhook-bad-token.yaml:
# I-5.b · a sender's token no longer matches DAEMON_WEBHOOK_TOKEN: pushes get a
# 401 and an access-log line only. Anyone who can reach the port can send a bad
# token, so this needs corroboration: refusals keep coming, no push gets in, AND
# pushes were accepted within the last 48 h (a real sender that stopped working).
# Reads the poller's webhook_rejections per endpoint and reason.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.webhook-bad-token
title: Pushes to the daemon webhook keep failing authentication
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-5, causes: [I-5.b]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  rejected:
    sample:
      signal: daemon_status.poller
      key: webhook_rejections
      by: [endpoint]
      labels: {reason: bad_token}
  accepted: {sample: {signal: daemon_status.poller, key: webhook_findings}}
group_by: [endpoint]
when:
  all:
    - {fn: increase, signal: rejected, window: 30m, op: ">=", value: {param: min_rejections}}
    - {fn: increase, signal: accepted, window: 30m, op: "==", value: 0}
    - {fn: increase, signal: accepted, window: 48h, op: ">", value: 0}
for: 10m
keep_firing_for: 15m
params:
  min_rejections: {type: number, default: 20, min: 1, max: 1000}
advice:
  summary: Pushes to the soc-daemon webhook keep being refused for a wrong token, and none has been accepted for 30 minutes, after pushes had been working.
  fix: >-
    Make the token the sender uses match DAEMON_WEBHOOK_TOKEN in the soc-daemon
    environment (one of them was likely rotated), then restart soc-daemon if you
    changed it there. If you don't expect any pushes, something else is probing
    port 8081: restrict who can reach it.
files.rules/ingest-webhook-token-unset.yaml:
# I-5.a · no DAEMON_WEBHOOK_TOKEN: the daemon webhook rejects every push with
# reason no_secret. Reads the poller's webhook_rejections per endpoint and reason.
# Outsider: anyone who can reach :8081 can trigger it, and "no
# token" is the default, so a site that doesn't use push can see it from a
# scanner (F7a-5); the threshold and the fix text are set for that.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: ingest.webhook-token-unset
title: Daemon webhook rejects every push because no token is set
revision: 1
fault: {class: ingest, mode: I-5, causes: [I-5.a]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  rejected:
    sample:
      signal: daemon_status.poller
      key: webhook_rejections
      by: [endpoint]
      labels: {reason: no_secret}
group_by: [endpoint]
when: {fn: increase, signal: rejected, window: 30m, op: ">=", value: {param: min_rejections}}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 30m
params:
  min_rejections: {type: number, default: 30, min: 1, max: 1000}
advice:
  summary: Something is pushing alerts to the soc-daemon webhook, and every push is refused because no webhook token is set.
  fix: >-
    Set DAEMON_WEBHOOK_TOKEN in the soc-daemon environment, restart soc-daemon,
    and give the same token to the sender. If you don't use push ingestion, block
    port 8081 from the senders instead.
files.rules/llm-budget-exhausted.yaml:
# L-5.a / L-5.c: Bifrost answered 402, gateway_retry raised BudgetExceeded
# (core/llm/gateway_retry.py:92-98) and the llm-worker logs it through report_outage
# (services/worker/jobs.py:101-112): once per tier, then every 100 refusals with a
# " (still failing, %d failures)" suffix. The first successful routed call logs
# "LLM budget available (%s tier)" (bare once per process, else "; recovered after %d
# failures", jobs.py:179-186). The tier is the first arg, so the latch is per tier and
# the rule is untrusted (keys read args), lane 2.
# Limit: the clear comes from a call that gets through, so on an idle install the
# incident stays open after the budget resets, until the next LLM call.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.budget-exhausted
title: The LLM spend budget is used up, so LLM calls are refused
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-5, causes: [L-5.a, L-5.c]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  spent:
    log:
      signal: log_llm_worker
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^LLM budget spent \(%s tier\); AI calls are refused until it resets( \(still failing, %d failures\))?$'}
      keys: {tier: "args[0]"}
  available:
    log:
      signal: log_llm_worker
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {re2: '^LLM budget available \(%s tier\)(; recovered after %d failures)?$'}
      keys: {tier: "args[0]"}
group_by: [tier]
when: {fn: latch, set: spent, clear: available}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The LLM gateway refused calls because a spend budget is used up, so triage and other LLM work fail until it resets.
  fix: >-
    In Bifrost, check the virtual key's budget (and any team or customer budget
    above it). Raise the budget, or wait for its period to reset. Vigil's work
    resumes on its own once calls are accepted again.
files.rules/llm-calls-failing.yaml:
# Catch-all for sustained llm-worker failures the specific rules don't name: Bifrost
# 5xx, request-conversion errors for new model families (L-1.j), Bifrost can't reach
# Ollama (L-4.b). Specific rules suppress it (suppression.yaml). The class list is an
# allowlist of path failures: it leaves out PromptInjectionBlocked and plain
# BadRequestError (alert content can trigger both, e.g. an oversized finding), keeping
# only the 400s that name a request-shape fault. Classes a specific rule names (budget,
# auth, rate limit, NotFound) aren't counted: those rules cover them. 15 m hold on a 5 m window (K1 T-07).
# Lane 3: unknown cause, escalate. Untrusted (args).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.calls-failing
title: Many LLM calls are failing for a reason Medic can't name
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-4, causes: [L-1.j, L-4.b]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  failed:
    log:
      signal: llm_worker_errors_as_success
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'llm_call failed (returning error dict): %s'}
      args: {"0": {re2: '^(InternalServerError|APIConnectionError|APITimeoutError|APIStatusError|ConnectError|ConnectTimeout|ReadTimeout|RemoteProtocolError|HTTPStatusError|TimeoutError): |^BadRequestError: .*(?i:not supported|failed to convert)'}}
params:
  calls: {type: number, default: 5, min: 3, max: 1000}
when: {fn: count, signal: failed, window: 5m, op: ">=", value: {param: calls}}
for: 15m
keep_firing_for: 10m
advice:
  summary: Possible LLM path fault. Many LLM calls have failed for 10 minutes or more, with errors Medic has no specific rule for.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident. As a
    workaround, assign triage and chat_default to a different model or provider in
    Settings, AI Config and see whether the failures stop. Record what you did.
files.rules/llm-cost-cap-paused.yaml:
# L-5.d: the orchestrator's hourly cost cap paused intake. Policy, not a fault (B5).
# The cap fails closed: hourly_paused is also true when the spend read fails (D1).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.cost-cap-paused
title: The hourly LLM cost cap has paused new investigations
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-5, causes: [L-5.d]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  paused: {sample: {signal: orchestrator_status, key: cost.hourly_paused}}
when: {fn: latest, signal: paused, op: "==", value: true}
for: 5m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The orchestrator has paused new investigations because the hourly LLM cost cap was reached. This is a policy setting, not a fault.
  fix: >-
    Raise max_total_hourly_cost in the orchestrator settings, or wait for the next
    hour. If spend is clearly below the cap, the spend read itself is failing (the
    cap pauses when it can't read spend): check that Postgres is up.
files.rules/llm-gateway-unreachable.yaml:
# L-4.a / L-4.c: the backend can't reach Bifrost (core/llm/bifrost/mirror.py:290-297,
# #1689; the mirror reconcile runs on every catalogue refresh, services/api/main.py:300-312).
# core/llm/outage.py appends to the caller's literal: set on the entry ERROR or its
# " (still failing, %d failures)" reminder; clear on "<healthy>; recovered after %d
# failures" or the bare healthy line a process logs on its first success. A restart
# during the outage keeps the latch set, since the new process re-reports at once.
# The backend runs 2 uvicorn workers on one log stream: one worker's first healthy
# line can clear another's outage, and reminders come only every 100 failures.
# All #1689 latches need INFO lines: a site that raises the log level above INFO never
# logs the clear, and its latches stay set.
# Lane 2: B5 says lane 1 for bundled Bifrost, but log lines alone can't route there.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.gateway-unreachable
title: The backend can't reach the LLM gateway (Bifrost)
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-4, causes: [L-4.a, L-4.c]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  down:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.llm.bifrost.mirror}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^Mirror reconcile skipped — Bifrost unreachable: %s( \(still failing, %d failures\))?$'}
  up:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.llm.bifrost.mirror}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {re2: '^Bifrost reachable for mirror reconcile(; recovered after %d failures)?$'}
when: {fn: latch, set: down, clear: up}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The backend can't reach Bifrost, the LLM gateway, so LLM calls and provider changes fail.
  fix: >-
    Check that Bifrost is running and that BIFROST_URL resolves from the backend
    (Compose: the bifrost container; host-native: http://localhost:8080; Helm: the
    gateway URL you configured). If Bifrost is up, check its own log for errors
    reaching the model provider (network egress, proxy, or for Ollama the
    OLLAMA_URL and, on Linux Compose, host.docker.internal mapped to the host
    gateway).
files.rules/llm-model-substituted.yaml:
# L-1.h: core/llm/target.py:52-90 swaps or force-sends a model the provider can't serve
# (WARNING; the swap logs once per provider-model pair per process). Read from soc-daemon
# only: triage resolves configured assignments there, while the backend's chat route
# passes the request's own model in (services/api/routers/claude.py:302-329), so any
# logged-in user could trigger the backend's line. L-1.i: the llm-worker can't find the
# provider and quietly uses ClaudeService (jobs.py:160-163, per call). Trusted.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.model-substituted
title: Vigil is sending LLM calls to a different model or provider than the one assigned
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-1, causes: [L-1.h, L-1.i]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  provider_missing:
    log:
      signal: log_llm_worker
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {eq: 'Provider %s not found; falling back to ClaudeService'}
  daemon_swap:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: core.llm.target}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {prefix: 'Provider %s cannot serve '}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: count, signal: provider_missing, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 1}
    - {fn: count, signal: daemon_swap, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 1}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: Vigil substituted a model or provider for the one assigned, because the assigned one can't serve the call or no longer exists.
  fix: >-
    Open Settings, AI Config and check each assignment (chat_default, triage and
    the others) points at an active provider and a model that provider serves.
    Re-activate or reassign any provider that was deleted or deactivated. Vigil
    logs a swap once per process, so a swap alert clears after an hour even if
    nothing changed: check the assignments either way. A provider that can't serve
    its own default model is logged on every call and keeps this open.
files.rules/llm-model-unservable.yaml:
# L-1.b/c/d/e: the model Vigil sends can't serve chat: no key supports it, it's an
# embedding model, it's retired, or it was removed. Seen in the worker's error dict
# text (args[0], so untrusted). I1 live eval cell L-1.c (embedding model assigned).
# Bifrost's 400 for a model no key serves reads "no keys found for provider: P and
# model: M" (type no_key_supports_model), seen live with a provider that has no key.
# A bare NotFoundError can also be a wrong BIFROST_URL path; the fix text says so.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.model-unservable
title: The model Vigil uses for LLM calls can't serve them
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-1, causes: [L-1.b, L-1.c, L-1.d, L-1.e]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  unservable:
    log:
      signal: llm_worker_errors_as_success
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'llm_call failed (returning error dict): %s'}
      args: {"0": {re2: '^NotFoundError: |(?i:does not support chat|no_key_supports_model|no keys found for provider|no keys found that support model|is no longer available|model_not_found|model not found|not found, try pulling)'}}
params:
  calls: {type: number, default: 2, min: 1, max: 100}
when: {fn: count, signal: unservable, window: 30m, op: ">=", value: {param: calls}}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: LLM calls fail because the assigned model can't serve chat (no key for it, an embedding model, or retired by the provider).
  fix: >-
    Open Settings, AI Config. Assign chat_default and triage to a chat-capable
    model that a provider with a working key serves. Then open Settings, LLM
    providers and check each active provider's default model is current and
    chat-capable (not an embedding model). If the models look right, check that
    BIFROST_URL points at Bifrost itself: a wrong path also answers not found.
files.rules/llm-provider-key-unusable.yaml:
# L-2.a: the provider rejects the key (worker error text; admin.py:180 "key stored but
# reports status"). L-2.c: a key write to Bifrost returned 4xx/5xx (admin.py:238).
# L-2.g: no API key reached the worker (jobs.py:86; may be a DB outage in disguise).
# L-2.h's line (admin.py:503) is left out: it repeats on every catalogue refresh for
# any active keyless row, so it would hold an incident open on dormant rows.
# Untrusted: the rejection is matched in args[0] (provider error text).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.provider-key-unusable
title: An LLM provider key is missing, rejected or never reached the gateway
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-2, causes: [L-2.a, L-2.c, L-2.g]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  rejected:
    log:
      signal: llm_worker_errors_as_success
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'llm_call failed (returning error dict): %s'}
      args: {"0": {re2: '^(AuthenticationError|PermissionDeniedError): |(?i:invalid x-api-key|incorrect api key|invalid api key|api key not valid)'}}
  no_key:
    log:
      signal: llm_worker_errors_as_success
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'llm_call failed (returning error dict): Empty response (model=%s; ClaudeService returned None - is an API key configured?)'}
  bad_status:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.llm.bifrost.admin}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'Bifrost: provider %s key stored but reports status=%s (%s)'}
  push_failed:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.llm.bifrost.admin}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {eq: 'Bifrost: %s %s returned %s: %s'}
params:
  calls: {type: number, default: 3, min: 1, max: 100}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: count, signal: rejected, window: 15m, op: ">=", value: {param: calls}}
    - {fn: count, signal: no_key, window: 15m, op: ">=", value: {param: calls}}
    - {fn: count, signal: bad_status, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 1}
    - {fn: count, signal: push_failed, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 1}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: An LLM provider key is missing, was rejected by the provider, or never reached the Bifrost gateway, so LLM calls fail.
  fix: >-
    Open Settings, LLM providers. Re-enter the key for the provider in use, test
    it, and confirm the provider shows as routable. If the provider rejects the
    key, replace it with a current one from the provider's console. If saving the
    key fails, check that Bifrost is running and reachable from the backend. If no
    key is found although one is saved, check that Postgres is up first: key
    lookup fails the same way when the database is down.
files.rules/llm-rate-limited.yaml:
# L-7.a: upstream 429s survive gateway_retry (core/llm/gateway_retry.py:105-112) and
# reach the worker's error dict. An outsider can raise LLM call volume by sending
# findings (webhooks), so the advice says "possible" and the rule needs 10 minutes of
# persistence (K1 T-07): a 5 m window under a 15 m hold, so it takes over 10 minutes of
# failures to fire.
# Untrusted (args).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.rate-limited
title: The LLM provider is rate-limiting Vigil's calls
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-7, causes: [L-7.a]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  limited:
    log:
      signal: llm_worker_errors_as_success
      logger: {eq: services.worker.jobs}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'llm_call failed (returning error dict): %s'}
      args: {"0": {re2: '^RateLimitError: |Error code: 429'}}
  worker_exhausted:
    log:
      signal: log_llm_worker
      logger: {eq: core.llm.gateway_retry}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {eq: 'gateway retries exhausted: last status %s after %d attempts'}
      args: {"0": {eq: "429"}}
  backend_exhausted:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.llm.gateway_retry}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {eq: 'gateway retries exhausted: last status %s after %d attempts'}
      args: {"0": {eq: "429"}}
params:
  calls: {type: number, default: 3, min: 1, max: 1000}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: count, signal: limited, window: 5m, op: ">=", value: {param: calls}}
    - {fn: count, signal: worker_exhausted, window: 5m, op: ">=", value: {param: calls}}
    - {fn: count, signal: backend_exhausted, window: 5m, op: ">=", value: {param: calls}}
for: 15m
keep_firing_for: 10m
advice:
  summary: Possible LLM quota problem. The provider has rate-limited Vigil's LLM calls for 10 minutes or more, so some triage and LLM work fails.
  fix: >-
    Check the provider's rate limits and usage for the key Vigil uses, and raise
    the quota if you can. Otherwise lower Vigil's LLM concurrency, or assign a
    different model or provider for triage. A sudden burst of incoming findings
    can also cause this; check whether finding volume spiked.
files.rules/llm-triage-no-provider.yaml:
# No LLM provider resolves for triage, so soc-daemon skips AI triage
# (services/daemon/processor.py:831-837, #1689 pair). The cause is L-1.k (#2011, folded
# in here). Set: the entry ERROR or its " (still failing, %d failures)" reminder. Clear:
# "LLM provider configured; recovered after %d failures", or the bare line a process
# logs on its first resolved provider. Reads templates only, so trusted; lane 2 because
# B5 has no exact row for it (nearest L-1).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.triage-no-provider
title: No LLM provider is configured, so AI triage is skipped
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-1, causes: [L-1.k]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  missing:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^No LLM provider configured, AI triage is skipped until one is set up( \(still failing, %d failures\))?$'}
  configured:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {re2: '^LLM provider configured(; recovered after %d failures)?$'}
when: {fn: latch, set: missing, clear: configured}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: soc-daemon found no active LLM provider, so new findings are stored without AI triage.
  fix: >-
    Open Settings, LLM providers. Add a provider with a working API key (or a
    reachable Ollama), make sure it is active, and either make it the default or
    assign it to triage in Settings, AI Config. AI triage resumes with the next
    finding.
files.rules/llm-triage-queue-unavailable.yaml:
# L-3.d: Redis or the ARQ queue is unreachable, so nothing can submit LLM jobs.
# "LLM gateway" in these lines is the ARQ client get_llm_gateway() opens on Redis
# (core/llm/gateway/gateway.py:143-154), not Bifrost: L-3.d, not L-4.
# Three latches, each set on an entry ERROR or its " (still failing, %d failures)"
# reminder (core/llm/outage.py) and cleared by "<healthy>; recovered after %d failures"
# or the bare healthy line a process logs on its first success:
#   soc-daemon connect  (services/daemon/processor.py:781-790)
#   soc-daemon submit   (processor.py:852-865): a Redis error once connected
#   backend start       (services/api/main.py:326; gateway.py:154 is the clear)
# A fresh soc-daemon connects on its next finding, so a latch outlives a fix on an
# idle install until then. The backend line is a plain ERROR, once per start.
# Reads templates only: trusted, lane 2 (B5: 1 by ownership of Redis).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.triage-queue-unavailable
title: Vigil can't reach the LLM job queue, so AI triage and LLM calls are skipped
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-3, causes: [L-3.d]}
lane: 2
detection: event
signals:
  daemon_down:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^Failed to connect LLM gateway, AI triage is skipped until it connects: %s( \(still failing, %d failures\))?$'}
  daemon_up:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {re2: '^LLM gateway connected for AI triage(; recovered after %d failures)?$'}
  submit_down:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^LLM queue unreachable, AI triage is failing: %s( \(still failing, %d failures\))?$'}
  submit_up:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.processor}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {re2: '^LLM queue reachable, AI triage resumed(; recovered after %d failures)?$'}
  backend_down:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: services.api.main}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'LLM Gateway not available, LLM calls will fail until Redis and the ARQ worker are up: %s'}
  backend_up:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.llm.gateway.gateway}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {eq: LLMGateway initialized (connected to Redis)}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: latch, set: daemon_down, clear: daemon_up}
    - {fn: latch, set: submit_down, clear: submit_up}
    - {fn: latch, set: backend_down, clear: backend_up}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: soc-daemon or the backend can't connect to the LLM job queue in Redis, so findings are stored without AI triage and LLM calls fail.
  fix: >-
    Check that Redis is running and reachable from soc-daemon and the backend
    (Compose: the redis container; Helm: the Redis service; host-native: the local
    Redis), and that REDIS_URL and the Redis password match on every service. If
    you run your own Redis, check it with whoever operates it. When Redis is back,
    soc-daemon reconnects on the next finding; the backend reconnects on its next
    LLM call or restart.
files.rules/llm-worker-wedged.yaml:
# L-3.b: the llm-worker container runs but its health check (arq --check, #1691) fails,
# so LLM jobs queue with no consumer. arq --check also fails when Redis is down, where a
# worker restart wouldn't help, so the rule also needs the agent-worker ready: its
# /readyz is true only while its own Redis client is ready (services/agent/worker.ts:645-650),
# an independent read (another sensor, another service) that Redis is up. Trusted,
# three samples from two sensors: passes the lane-1 gate with real corroboration.
# Limits: "ready" means Redis is connected, not that it accepts writes, so a Redis
# refusing writes (MISCONF, OOM under noeviction) can still read as a wedge; a Redis
# write-health signal (redis_queues, D2-12) should be added before a runbook attaches.
# If the agent-worker is down, redis_ok is never true and a wedge goes unreported.
# Compose only: Helm's probes restart the pod themselves (#1499); host-native has no
# health check. Runbook: restart-llm-worker (runbooks/restart-llm-worker.yaml) is attached.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: llm.worker-wedged
title: The llm-worker is running but failing its health check
revision: 1
fault: {class: llm, mode: L-3, causes: [L-3.b]}
lane: 1
detection: event
shapes: [compose]
signals:
  state: {sample: {signal: containers, key: state, labels: {service: llm-worker}}}
  health: {sample: {signal: containers, key: health, labels: {service: llm-worker}}}
  redis_ok: {sample: {signal: agent_worker_readyz, key: ready}}
when:
  all:
    - {fn: latest, signal: state, op: "==", value: running}
    - {fn: latest, signal: health, op: "==", value: unhealthy}
    - {fn: latest, signal: redis_ok, op: "==", value: true}
for: 3m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The llm-worker container is running but has failed its health check for 3 minutes, so LLM jobs wait with nothing to take them.
  fix: >-
    Restart the llm-worker container (docker compose restart llm-worker). If it
    turns unhealthy again, check that Redis is up and accepting writes (its log
    shows MISCONF or OOM errors if not). Report it as a Vigil defect with this
    incident and attach the llm-worker log from before the restart.
files.rules/pipeline-agent-container-down.yaml:
# medic-core rule (F7c-agents). An agent-worker or agent-serve container that has
# stopped (exited, or dead) and stays stopped: compose restart: unless-stopped
# brings back a crash but not a container someone stopped or one that Docker gave up
# on. A crash loop reads "restarting", not "exited": that is
# pipeline.agent-container-restarting. A stopped container also leaves Docker's DNS,
# so the readiness sensors go blind (watcher.sensor-blind) rather than read
# ready=false: this rule is what names the stop, and nothing needs suppressing.
# Compose only: Helm's pod controller recreates a stopped pod itself, and a pod that
# stays down also fails the readiness rules.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.agent-container-down
title: An agent container has stopped
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 3
detection: event
shapes: [compose]
signals:
  worker: {sample: {signal: containers, key: state, labels: {service: agent-worker}}}
  serve: {sample: {signal: containers, key: state, labels: {service: agent-serve}}}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: latest, signal: worker, op: "==", value: exited}
    - {fn: latest, signal: worker, op: "==", value: dead}
    - {fn: latest, signal: serve, op: "==", value: exited}
    - {fn: latest, signal: serve, op: "==", value: dead}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The agent-worker or agent-serve container has been stopped for 2 minutes, so runs queue with no worker or chat and run status reads fail.
  fix: >-
    Check which container stopped (docker compose ps agent-worker agent-serve) and
    read its log (docker compose logs) for why. If nobody stopped it on purpose,
    start it again (docker compose up -d agent-worker agent-serve). If it stops
    again, report it as a Vigil defect with this incident. Record what you did.
files.rules/pipeline-agent-container-restartin:
# medic-core rule (F7c-agents). Docker restarted an agent-worker or agent-serve
# container on its own more than once in 5 minutes: a crash loop, usually from a
# bad environment value, a missing dependency or an out-of-memory kill. The cause
# isn't in the container's state, so lane 3.
# RestartCount counts only Docker's own restarts (not docker restart or compose
# up). The containers sensor gives each start its own counter epoch, so the engine
# adds the whole count at each restart: a container with no history needs two
# restarts to pass, one that restarted before needs only one.
# Compose only; Helm reads pods (pipeline.agent-pod-restarting).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.agent-container-restarting
title: An agent container keeps restarting
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 3
detection: event
shapes: [compose]
signals:
  worker: {sample: {signal: containers, key: restart_count, labels: {service: agent-worker}}}
  serve: {sample: {signal: containers, key: restart_count, labels: {service: agent-serve}}}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: increase, signal: worker, window: 5m, op: ">", value: 1}
    - {fn: increase, signal: serve, window: 5m, op: ">", value: 1}
for: 1m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The agent-worker or agent-serve container was restarted by Docker more than once in the last 5 minutes, so runs or chat reads keep being interrupted.
  fix: >-
    Read the log of the container that keeps restarting (docker compose logs
    agent-worker agent-serve), the last lines before each restart name the error,
    and check that Redis and Postgres are up and its environment values are set.
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident and the log. Record what you did.
files.rules/pipeline-agent-pod-restarting.yaml:
# medic-core rule (F7c-agents). The Helm twin of pipeline.agent-container-restarting:
# an agent-worker or agent-serve pod's containers restarted more than once in 5
# minutes (restartCount, for the pod's life: the sensor's epoch is the pod UID, so
# the increase is exact). The cause isn't in the pod's state, so lane 3.
# One series per pod (label pod): the rule groups by it, because without that several
# series are ambiguous_series and it would never fire. wiring.py groups only
# pipeline.agent-worker-not-ready at load, so the group is declared here.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.agent-pod-restarting
title: An agent pod keeps restarting
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 3
detection: event
shapes: [helm]
signals:
  worker: {sample: {signal: pods, key: restart_count, labels: {service: agent-worker}, by: [pod]}}
  serve: {sample: {signal: pods, key: restart_count, labels: {service: agent-serve}, by: [pod]}}
group_by: [pod]
when:
  any:
    - {fn: increase, signal: worker, window: 5m, op: ">", value: 1}
    - {fn: increase, signal: serve, window: 5m, op: ">", value: 1}
for: 1m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: An agent-worker or agent-serve pod restarted more than once in the last 5 minutes, so runs or chat reads keep being interrupted.
  fix: >-
    Read the previous log of the pod that keeps restarting (kubectl logs --previous
    on it) and its events (kubectl describe pod); they name the error or an
    out-of-memory kill. Check that Redis and Postgres are reachable. Report it as
    a Vigil defect with this incident and the log. Record what you did.
files.rules/pipeline-agent-reads-failing.yaml:
# P-1: reads of the agent service fail (core/agents/projections.py, _note_read). The
# ERROR is logged once when reads start failing; later failures are DEBUG until the
# INFO "agent service reads recovered", which is logged on a process's first
# successful read as well as on a success after a failure, so a restart after the
# fix clears the incident. The backend (workflows_router, case_brief,
# learning_episodes) and soc-daemon (distil_once -> read_distil) both import that
# module and each keeps its own _read_failing, so two latches: one per stream.
# Both failing-read templates are %-style catalog entries; the recovery is a
# constant-text catalog line. Latch-only. A latch clears on that process's next
# successful read, which on an idle install is the next run lookup. A healthy start
# logs one recovery with no earlier failure; a clear with no set leaves the latch false.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.agent-reads-failing
title: Vigil can't read run status from the agent service
revision: 2
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  backend_down:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.agents.projections}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^(could not read the %s for %s: %s|%s for %s answered %s)$'}
  backend_up:
    log:
      signal: log_backend
      logger: {eq: core.agents.projections}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {eq: agent service reads recovered}
  daemon_down:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: core.agents.projections}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {re2: '^(could not read the %s for %s: %s|%s for %s answered %s)$'}
  daemon_up:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: core.agents.projections}
      level: [INFO]
      template: {eq: agent service reads recovered}
when:
  any:
    - {fn: latch, set: backend_down, clear: backend_up}
    - {fn: latch, set: daemon_down, clear: daemon_up}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The backend or soc-daemon can't read run status from the agent service, so run progress, case briefs and learning reads come back empty.
  fix: >-
    Check that the agent service is running and that the backend and soc-daemon
    can reach it: AGENT_URL and AGENT_INTERNAL_TOKEN must match on all three
    (Compose: the agent-serve container; Helm: the agent Service). If a not-ready
    incident for agent-serve is open, fix that first. Otherwise report it as a
    Vigil defect with this incident and attach the backend log, which names the
    error. The incident clears on the first successful read of
    the service that logged the failure, including right after a restart, so on an
    idle install it can outlast the fix until the next run lookup.
files.rules/pipeline-agent-serve-not-ready.yam:
# medic-core rule (F7c-agents). The twin of pipeline.agent-worker-not-ready for
# agent-serve: its /readyz is true only while a SELECT 1 on its own Postgres pool
# succeeds (services/agent/serve.ts serveReady), so false means the chat and run
# projection surface the backend calls is up but can't reach its ledger, or is not
# answering at all (refused and timeout read false too). Which of those can't be
# told from /readyz alone, so: lane 3. Helm reaches serve through its Service, one
# series with no pod label, so no grouping. Silent where
# VIGIL_MEDIC_AGENT_SERVE_ADDR isn't set (no agent_serve_readyz series).
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.agent-serve-not-ready
title: The agent-serve service is running but not ready
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  ready: {sample: {signal: agent_serve_readyz, key: ready}}
when: {fn: latest, signal: ready, op: "==", value: false}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The agent-serve service has reported not ready for 2 minutes, so chat and run status reads that go through it fail.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident. Check that agent-serve can
    reach Postgres (its readiness is one query against it) and read its log for
    the error. Record what you did.
files.rules/pipeline-agent-worker-not-ready.ya:
# medic-core rule (S4 walking skeleton). P-1.j: the worker is up but /readyz says no.
# agent_worker_readyz.ready is false when its BullMQ worker isn't running or its
# Redis client isn't ready (services/agent/worker.ts:645-650), and for refused,
# timeout and 503 alike, so runs queue and nothing picks them up. The Redis lane
# depends on who runs Redis, so: lane 3 (S4-1).
# Compose and host-native publish one series and no pod label, so this file does
# not group. On Helm, load_medic_core groups the same rule by pod: several series
# would otherwise be ambiguous_series and this rule would never fire.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.agent-worker-not-ready
title: The agent worker is running but not ready
revision: 2
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1.j]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  ready: {sample: {signal: agent_worker_readyz, key: ready}}
when: {fn: latest, signal: ready, op: "==", value: false}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 5m
advice:
  summary: The agent worker has reported not ready for 2 minutes, so new investigation runs are queued but not picked up.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident. Check that
    the agent worker can reach Redis; restarting it reconnects only if Redis is
    up. Record what you did.
files.rules/pipeline-lease-sweep-failing.yaml:
# P-1: the agent worker's lease sweeper (services/agent/worker.ts:759) logs
# "sweep failed" at WARNING each tick (VIGIL_SWEEP_MS, default 30 s) while it can't
# read the lease table, so runs whose worker died are never reclaimed. An agent_json
# line, so the msg is untrusted and not in catalog.yaml. >= 10 in 10 min assumes a
# sweep interval <= 60 s. Lane 3: the table lives in Postgres or Redis, which the
# operator may or may not own.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.lease-sweep-failing
title: The agent worker can't sweep for abandoned runs
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 3
detection: event
input_trust: untrusted
signals:
  failed:
    log:
      signal: log_agent_worker
      logger: {eq: agent.worker}
      level: [WARNING]
      template: {eq: sweep failed}
      trusted_only: false
when: {fn: count, signal: failed, window: 10m, op: ">=", value: 10}
for: 5m
keep_firing_for: 10m
advice:
  summary: The agent worker's lease sweep fails on every pass, so runs whose worker died are never reclaimed and stay stuck as running.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident and attach the agent-worker
    log, which names the error. Check that the agent worker can reach its lease
    store (Postgres and Redis). Until it is fixed, cancel runs that have been
    executing for a long time by hand in the console.
files.rules/pipeline-processor-errors.yaml:
# P-4.d / P-4.e · the processor keeps failing items: worker errors, per-finding
# errors and triage results it can't persist all add to /status processor.errors.
# LLM failures count too; suppression.yaml makes this a child of class-llm
# incidents (mode P-4). Malformed pushed findings raise errors as well, hence
# lane 3 and a floor of 10 in 15 min.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.processor-errors
title: The soc-daemon processor keeps failing findings
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-4, causes: [P-4.d, P-4.e]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  errors: {sample: {signal: daemon_status.processor, key: errors}}
when: {fn: increase, signal: errors, window: 15m, op: ">=", value: {param: min_errors}}
for: 10m
keep_firing_for: 15m
params:
  min_errors: {type: number, default: 10, min: 1, max: 10000}
advice:
  summary: The soc-daemon processor has failed at least 10 findings in 15 minutes; failed findings are not triaged or stored correctly.
  fix: >-
    Check that Postgres is healthy and has free disk. If it is, report it as a
    Vigil defect with this incident and attach the soc-daemon log.
files.rules/pipeline-run-enqueue-failed.yaml:
# P-1: the daemon's run enqueue is refused (services/daemon/orchestrator.py:1631), so
# the hunt or investigation never starts and its run is marked failed. The enqueue
# is a BullMQ add on Redis (core/agents/queue.py), so an unreachable Redis or a wrong
# Redis password lands here, and so does any other error from the queue call. A
# %-style line, so a catalog template: trusted. Matches this template only; "could
# not enqueue shadow adjudication for %s: %s" (:1656) is a different line and not a
# run. Lane 3: the cause can't be told from the line.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.run-enqueue-failed
title: The daemon can't start agent runs
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 3
detection: event
signals:
  failed:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.orchestrator}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {eq: 'could not enqueue %s: %s'}
when: {fn: count, signal: failed, window: 10m, op: ">=", value: 1}
for: 2m
keep_firing_for: 10m
advice:
  summary: soc-daemon was refused when it tried to queue an agent run, so that run never started and was marked failed.
  fix: >-
    Check that Redis is running and reachable from soc-daemon (Compose: the redis
    container; Helm: the Redis service; host-native: the local Redis), and that
    REDIS_URL and the Redis password on soc-daemon match the ones the agent worker
    uses. If both look right, report it as a Vigil defect with this incident and
    attach the soc-daemon log, which names the error. Re-run the affected
    investigation once it is fixed.
files.rules/pipeline-runs-url-unset.yaml:
# P-1: the agent worker started without VIGIL_RUNS_URL (services/agent/worker.ts:792),
# so run progress isn't mirrored to the backend and checkpoints can't be answered.
# The ERROR is logged ONCE per start, and "agent worker started" follows it whether
# the mirror is on or off, so no line clears it. agent_json, so untrusted and not in
# catalog.yaml. The count holds the incident open for the 1h window plus
# keep_firing_for 24h (about 25 h) after a start with the URL unset, then it
# resolves on its own even if the worker is still running unfixed: nothing logs
# again until the next start. A restart with the URL set does not clear it early;
# a restart without it logs again and extends the hold. Lane 2: the fix is in the
# operator's environment.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.runs-url-unset
title: The agent worker was started without VIGIL_RUNS_URL
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-1, causes: [P-1]}
lane: 2
detection: event
input_trust: untrusted
signals:
  unset:
    log:
      signal: log_agent_worker
      logger: {eq: agent.worker}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {prefix: 'VIGIL_RUNS_URL is unset'}
      trusted_only: false
when: {fn: count, signal: unset, window: 1h, op: ">=", value: 1}
for: 0s
keep_firing_for: 24h
advice:
  summary: The agent worker started without VIGIL_RUNS_URL, so the console doesn't see run progress and runs that ask for a checkpoint can't be answered.
  fix: >-
    Set VIGIL_RUNS_URL on the agent worker to the backend's runs address
    (Compose: the agent-worker service environment; Helm: the agent worker's
    values; host-native: the shell that starts it), then restart the agent worker.
    Medic can't see the fix: this incident resolves about 25 hours after the
    worker's start line, whether or not you fixed it, so check the worker's
    start-up log for the "VIGIL_RUNS_URL is unset" line to confirm.
# P-2.a · the orchestrator's supervision loop raises every tick (30 s at the
# default loop_interval 60), so no stale or cost kill runs. The line is an
# f-string with the exception text (orchestrator.py:1456), so untrusted and
# not in catalog.yaml. >= 10 in 10 min assumes ORCHESTRATOR_LOOP_INTERVAL <= 120 s.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.supervision-loop-failing
title: The orchestrator's run supervisor keeps failing
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-2, causes: [P-2.a]}
lane: 3
detection: event
input_trust: untrusted
signals:
  failed:
    log:
      signal: log_soc_daemon
      logger: {eq: services.daemon.orchestrator}
      level: [ERROR]
      template: {prefix: 'Supervision loop error: '}
      trusted_only: false
when: {fn: count, signal: failed, window: 10m, op: ">=", value: 10}
for: 5m
keep_firing_for: 10m
advice:
  summary: The orchestrator's run supervisor fails on every pass, so stuck or over-budget runs are never stopped.
  fix: >-
    Report it as a Vigil defect with this incident and attach the soc-daemon
    log. Until it is fixed, check the console for runs that have been executing
    for a long time and cancel them by hand.
files.rules/pipeline-triage-stalled.yaml:
# P-4.a/b/c · findings are processed but none is triaged. The LLM path is the
# usual cause (P-4.a): suppression.yaml makes this a child of any class-llm
# incident, so the LLM fault shows instead. With DAEMON_AUTO_TRIAGE off triage
# never runs by design, so the rule needs auto_triage_enabled from /status.
apiVersion: medic.rules/v1
kind: Rule
id: pipeline.triage-stalled
title: Findings are processed but none are triaged
revision: 1
fault: {class: pipeline, mode: P-4, causes: [P-4.a, P-4.b, P-4.c]}
lane: 3
detection: absence
signals:
  processed: {sample: {signal: daemon_status.processor, key: processed}}
  triaged:   {sample: {signal: daemon_status.processor, key: triaged}}
  auto:      {sample: {signal: daemon_status.processor, key: auto_triage_enabled}}
when:
  all:
    - {fn: latest, signal: auto, op: "==", value: true}
    - {fn: increase, signal: processed, window: 30m, op: ">=", value: {param: min_processed}}
    - {fn: increase, signal: triaged, window: 30m, op: "==", value: 0}
for: 10m
keep_firing_for: 30m
params:
  min_processed: {type: number, default: 5, min: 1, max: 1000}
advice:
  summary: Findings are being stored, but AI triage has completed none in 30 minutes.
  fix: >-
    Check the LLM path (Settings, LLM providers and the Bifrost gateway). If the
    LLM path is healthy, report it as a Vigil defect with this incident and
    attach the soc-daemon log.
files.runbooks/restart-llm-worker.yaml:
# Descriptor only: Phase 0 runs nothing. The router copies {id, verify_after_s} onto
# a lane-1 incident for each rule in applies_to, and would_have names this runbook.
apiVersion: medic.runbooks/v1
kind: Runbook
id: restart-llm-worker
title: Restart the llm-worker container
applies_to: [llm.worker-wedged]
action: {type: restart_service, service: llm-worker}
verify_after_s: 300
description: >-
  Restarts the llm-worker container so it takes LLM jobs from the queue again.
  Medic checks five minutes later that the worker passes its health check; if it
  is still unhealthy, the incident stays open for an admin.
